quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What should you do if you become tired while driving?

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or change drivers. Tiredness slows your reactions and makes you less alert. This makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: Before you back up your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check behind the vehicle before getting in.
Depend entirely on your mirrors.
Accelerate quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before getting in.
questions.explanation: Check behind the vehicle before getting in. Children and small objects may be hidden from your view in the driver's seat.

questions.question: You see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and the signal arm extended. What should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Go 15 mph if no children are present.
Drive at normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: You must come to a full stop and stay stopped until the signal arm is pulled back and the bus moves. This rule applies whether you are going the same direction as the bus or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing you.
Cars coming toward you.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward you.
questions.explanation: You must yield to cars coming straight toward you. You can only turn left when it is safe and does not affect oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you is stopped in your lane with red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have exited.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop while the red lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop while the red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stay stopped as long as the red lights are flashing. You can go when the lights stop flashing. If the bus is on the other side of a divided highway, you do not need to stop.

questions.question: You have an argument and feel angry. What should you do before driving?

options.text: Play loud music so you do not think about it.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the interstate to calm down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect your driving safety. If you are angry, excited, afraid, worried, or sad, calm down before driving. You need to focus on the road, not on what upset you.

questions.question: Which statement is true about large trucks?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger cars.
All trucks have air brakes that stop them quickly.
They turn easier than passenger cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than passenger cars. A passenger car at 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck at 55 mph can need almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit between a turning truck or bus and the curb. You could have a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.

questions.question: A school bus ahead is stopped to load or unload children. What must you do?

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
questions.explanation: Stop when the bus has flashing lights and the stop arm extended. Stay stopped until the lights stop flashing and the arm is pulled in. After the bus moves, make sure no children are crossing the road before you go.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle on your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you are far enough ahead before returning to your lane. When you can see both of the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return safely.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, what should you do?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. The water may hide dangers you cannot see. If you find a flooded area, turn around and find a different route.

questions.question: When should you change lanes?

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully. Only change lanes when you need to. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: What should you do if you must make an emergency stop on an interstate?

options.text: Sound your horn at passing cars.
Get out of your car and flag down the first vehicle that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your car if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your car if you can.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on an interstate shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay in your car if you can. Interstate traffic moves very fast, making it unsafe to stand or walk on the shoulder.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Drive at your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: When entering a work zone, slow down and be ready to stop. Follow posted speed limits and stay alert. Workers may be present.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Slow down to avoid collisions and brake damage.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates are raised.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates are raised.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when gates are lowered or warning lights are flashing. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: Why is night driving more dangerous than day driving?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead due to darkness and headlight glare. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Stay farther back than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than normal.
questions.explanation: Keep a three- to four-second distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. Extra distance helps protect you both if the rider falls. This is especially important on wet roads, gravel, and metal surfaces.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Pull to the right and go around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before you proceed.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.
Tailgate the driver in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on your driving. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Allow extra time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off the weather and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Before driving after taking medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor if the medicine affects driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor if the medicine affects driving.
questions.explanation: Medicine can affect your ability to drive safely. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how any medicine may affect your driving. This is especially important for prescription tranquilizers or sedatives.

questions.question: If your tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, take your foot off the accelerator and slow down gradually. Don't brake hard until the vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: In work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you quickly.
Keep a safe distance and avoid tailgating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and avoid tailgating.
questions.explanation: In work zones, stay far away from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Keep more space between your car and the car ahead. Never tailgate.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses after the "Don't Walk" signal starts flashing. They are in the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Proceed because you have the right-of-way.
Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait for the pedestrian to cross before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrian to cross before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a green light, give the right-of-way to any vehicle, bike, or pedestrian in the intersection. If a pedestrian is crossing, wait until they finish before you drive.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and lower visibility.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver won't expect you there and may move onto the shoulder, causing a crash.

questions.question: Work zone signs and equipment are:

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Drive carefully when you see orange warning signs.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across.
Always.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes (with or without a red tip).

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow, turn on your:

options.text: Dashboard lights.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you can't see clearly or when other drivers can't see you. Use low beams whenever you need your windshield wipers.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and pass cars often, you will:

options.text: Get to your destination much faster and safer.
Increase your chances of a crash.
Help reduce traffic jams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your chances of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing other vehicles on two-lane roads. Each time you pass another vehicle, your risk of a crash goes up.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you:

options.text: Are coming to a railroad crossing and should get ready to stop.
Will always stop at the railroad crossing ahead.
Should stop and wait for a signal before crossing the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are coming to a railroad crossing and should get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign shows you are coming to a railroad crossing. Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you go forward.

questions.question: A distraction when driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to make a sudden move while driving.
Anything that takes your focus away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your focus away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your focus away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. Distracted driving can cause crashes that lead to damage, injury, and death.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are coming.
Yield to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. These signs tell drivers that bicycles may be crossing in this area.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: The only way to sober up is to give your body time to remove the alcohol from your system. Nothing else, including food and drinks, can speed up this process.

questions.question: If you drive slower than the traffic flow, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and get a ticket.
Help traffic move better.
Show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must drive slower during heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you block the normal flow of traffic by driving too slowly, you may get a ticket. You should match the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: The flashing red lights and stop arm on a school bus turn on when the bus is picking up or dropping off students. When you see these signals, you cannot go forward until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC number means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are generally:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have an orange background with black letters or symbols. These signs are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.
